24 The sound from a loudspeaker placed above a tube causes resonance of the air in the tube.
A stationary wave is formed with two nodes and two antinodes as shown.
loudspeaker
60 cm
The speed of sound in the air is 340 m s–1.
What is the frequency of the sound?
A
430 Hz
B
570 Hz
C
850 Hz
D
1700 Hz

hints: Notice the tube has an open top under the loudspeaker and a closed bottom, so displacement has an antinode at the top and a node at the bottom.
Count the node to antinode sections in the 60 cm diagram: two nodes and two antinodes means three $\lambda/4$ sections fit in the tube.
Use $L = 3\lambda/4$ to find $\lambda$ from $0.60\text{ m}$, then use $v = f\lambda$ with $v = 340\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Identify the ends: the top is open to the air so it is a displacement antinode, and the closed bottom is a displacement node.
Recall the spacing rule: the distance from a node to the next antinode is $\lambda/4$.
Count sections in the 60 cm length: from the top antinode to first node is $\lambda/4$, then to the next antinode and node adds another $\lambda/2$, so $L = 3\lambda/4$.
Calculate the frequency: $f = v/\lambda = 340/0.80 = 425\text{ Hz} \approx 430\text{ Hz}$.

A.explanation: With $L = 3\lambda/4 = 0.60\text{ m}$, $\lambda = 0.80\text{ m}$ and $f = v/\lambda = 425\text{ Hz} \approx 430\text{ Hz}$.

B.explanation: This uses $\lambda = 0.60\text{ m}$, giving $f = 340/0.60 \approx 570\text{ Hz}$, which ignores the $3\lambda/4$ pattern.

C.explanation: This uses $\lambda = 0.40\text{ m}$, giving $f = 850\text{ Hz}$, which treats the 60 cm length as $1.5$ wavelengths.

D.explanation: This uses $\lambda = 0.20\text{ m}$, giving $f = 1700\text{ Hz}$, which treats each node to antinode section as $\lambda/2$ instead of $\lambda/4$.
